name: amigit
readme:
Short:        Local-only git client for AmigaOS 3.x
Type:         dev/misc
Architecture: m68k-amigaos >= 68020
Uploader:     duncan@bowring.us
Author:       Duncan Bowring (amiport, built on libgit2)
Version:      0.1-3
URL:          https://github.com/bdgscotland/amiport

amigit -- Local-only git client for AmigaOS 3.x

An amiport-native git CLI built on libgit2 1.8.5. Local repositories
only; no network commands (no clone/fetch/push/pull/remote). Covers
the v1 ten-command core: version, init, status, log, show, diff,
add, commit, checkout, branch, tag. Upstream git is infeasible on
AmigaOS because its command dispatch is built on fork()/execvp(),
which AmigaOS does not provide; libgit2 is embedded directly into
the binary instead.

What's new in 0.1-3:
  - Friendly init error now also fires for explicit-path init on
    a multi-character volume (e.g. 'amigit init WORK:playground'),
    not just bare 'amigit init' from a CWD. Pre-0.1-3, the explicit-
    path case fell through to libgit2's cryptic './.' error. The
    error message now points at the AmigaDOS Assign workaround.
    See PORT.md for the engineering notes -- three real-fix
    approaches were tried in this session and rolled back.

Known limitations:
  - No network commands. clone/fetch/push/pull/remote/submodule
    require bsdsocket + libssh2/http-shim -- a future Phase 4.
  - No merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert, or stash.
  - No interactive flows (add -i, rebase -i, commit --amend with
    editor). AmigaOS has no portable $EDITOR integration.
  - Commit messages via -m must be a single shell token; -F <file>
    (multi-line) is planned for a future release.
  - 'amigit init' on multi-character volume names ('WORK:',
    'Ram Disk:', 'System 3.1:') produces a friendly error pointing
    at the AmigaDOS Assign workaround. libgit2's path-root
    recognizer only handles single-character drive prefixes.
    Workaround: 'Assign R: WORK: ; amigit init R:foo'.
  - No color output, no pager integration.

Binary: ~1.05 MB. Stack: 256 KB. Requires 4 MB free RAM at runtime.
68020 minimum -- no plain 68000/A500 support.
porting_notes: First working git client for AmigaOS 3.x. Written from scratch as an amiport-native CLI on top of the pruned lib/libgit2/libgit2.a (1.8.5) because upstream git's fork()/execvp()-based command dispatch is structurally infeasible on 68k AmigaOS. Implements the PDR-010a v1 ten-command core: version, init, status, log, show, diff, add, commit, checkout, branch, tag. 0.1-3 widens the friendly-error coverage to include explicit-multi-char-volume-path init (e.g. 'amigit init WORK:playground') in addition to the bare-CWD case from 0.1-2 -- both are now caught and produce the same actionable workaround message instead of libgit2's cryptic './.' error. Three real-fix approaches were tried in the 0.1-3 session and rolled back: (1) libgit2 dos_drive_prefix_length patch + amigit slash-injection regressed 20 in-repo tests because libnix and libgit2 disagree on whether 'Ram Disk:/foo' stat-equals 'Ram Disk:foo'; (2) chdir-then-init dance failed because libgit2 absolutizes '.' early via realpath; (3) manual init bypass via direct mkdir+fopen caused unrelated test 29 to hang on FS-UAE -- root cause not diagnosed in-session. The friendly-error approach is the working compromise. 82/82 FS-UAE functional tests pass.
known_limitations: No network commands (clone/fetch/push/pull/remote) -- requires bsdsocket + libssh2 or http-shim in a future Phase 4. No merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert, or stash. No interactive flows (rebase -i, add -i, commit --amend with editor). Commit messages via -m must be single shell tokens; -F <file> (multi-line from file) is planned for a future release. 'amigit init' on multi-character volume names ('WORK:', 'Ram Disk:', 'System 3.1:') produces a friendly error -- workaround is to AmigaDOS Assign a single-letter alias and init against that ('Assign R: WORK: ; amigit init R:foo'). libgit2's git_fs_path_root only recognizes single-character ASCII drive prefixes. No color output, no pager integration. Empty initial commits rejected (no --allow-empty). Requires 4 MB free RAM at runtime. 68020 minimum -- no plain 68000/A500 support.
